verdict.rationale: Reader documents a headless-Chrome fetching engine (`x-engine: browser`), a `x-wait-for-selector` header for dynamic content, and browser-locale rendering, so it can render JS-heavy pages. However, the evidence never shows it returning the fully rendered HTML: `x-respond-with` is documented only with a Markdown/frontmatter option, and the product is positioned around LLM-friendly text. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of a raw rendered-HTML output mode, independent or hands-on confirmation of SPA rendering quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can render JavaScript-heavy single-page applications and get the fully rendered HTML

citations.quote: `x-engine` — enforces a fetching engine: `browser` (headless Chrome), `curl` (lightweight, no JS), or `auto`
sets the browser locale used when rendering
It bundles headless Chrome, LibreOffice, and CJK fonts
